brief: An AI travel assistant that helps people plan and navigate trips.
offer: Build and edit an itinerary, combine travellers' preferences, organise booking details and suggest changes during the trip. Users verify recommendations and approve bookings. No autonomous purchases or human concierge are included. Price: £30 per trip, paid by this traveller. No free trial. Existing free tools remain available. Product benefits have not been demonstrated.
question: For your next trip, choose between this paid assistant, continuing with your existing free tools, or neither. Explain the trade-off using only your stated workflow. Do not assume unproven time savings, accuracy or capabilities.

sources.title: Booking.com Global AI Sentiment Report
sources.observation: Booking.com reports five general AI attitude cohorts: AI Enthusiasts are interested in AI possibilities; AI Advocates promote benefits and responsible adoption; AI Cautious are wary of AI development or use; AI Skeptics express scepticism; AI Detractors resist adoption. Its online survey covered 37,325 respondents in 33 markets in April and May 2025. These are aggregate general-AI attitudes, not travel-product purchasing segments. The report identifies travel tasks including destination research, local activities, restaurant suggestions, translation and transport navigation. It also describes widespread verification of AI output and limited comfort with autonomous decisions. Neither the cohorts nor task interest establish willingness to pay for this assistant.
sources.limit: Aggregate published research; no paid-demand evidence

sources.title: Expedia Group AI Trust Gap
sources.observation: Expedia Group reports a gap between AI-assisted travel planning and trust in booking. YouGov surveyed more than 5,700 adults in the US, UK and India during March 2026. Reported uses include travel suggestions, price monitoring and itinerary building. Search engines and online travel agencies remain common planning alternatives. The report highlights control, payment-data privacy, misuse of personal data and customer support as concerns about AI transactions. Trusted travel brands are preferred by many respondents for booking. This industry-commissioned survey describes stated attitudes; it does not establish demand for a paid standalone travel assistant.
sources.limit: Aggregate published research; no paid-demand evidence
